scope: Bucket-local delta-varint compression of immutable filename postings; no deployed service, configuration, ACL or index-file changes by this subtask.
official_findings: Everything documents a RAM-resident runtime database saved at exit, with name/path mandatory and several metadata indexes optional.
Everything db_compress publicly documents Bzip 2 database compression and a CPU-versus-I/O loading/saving tradeoff.
Everything FAQ gives example sizes (one million files: about 100 MB RAM and 45 MB disk); user/Pulse/Everything indexed data equivalence was not established.
No unpublished Everything.db structure was read or inferred.

implementation.encoding: 65537 uint32 byte offsets per table; bucket-local strictly increasing IDs stored as canonical unsigned delta LEB128.
implementation.query: mmap and decode selected bucket only; no table-sized decompression heap or query semantics removed.
implementation.startup_integrity: Full bounded bucket/varint validation; rejects truncated, noncanonical, overflow, nonmonotonic, out-of-node-range and section-crossing data. Existing manifest CRC validation/A-B/WAL strategy unchanged.
implementation.writer_peak: Build and encode the two raw posting tables sequentially, releasing each raw ID array before constructing the next.
implementation.offline_converter: --convert ABS_INPUT ABS_ABSENT_OUTPUT uses production mapping/writing; preserves built timestamp, node/attribute/name-pool/child-order/FRN bytes, volume checkpoints and every posting ID; only output.tmp and then specified output are written, no Engine.Start/TryLoadCache/AdoptMapped, no service or manifest mutation.

build.initial_issue: First storage publication failure was stale index_shard.cpp.obj retaining version 11 due missing header rebuild dependency. All affected index_shard.cpp objects were explicitly recompiled; final directed storage suite passed. No test was removed or weakened.

checks: real-v11 complete read and v12 write
all core sections compared byte-for-byte and hashed
all single-char and bigram posting IDs compared bucket-by-bucket
real same-FRN USN rename/create/delete, including BMP CJK and surrogate pair
real per-volume WAL bytes and hashes exactly match across encodings
mixed v12 active to v11 previous A/B fallback
valid v11 does not trigger encoding-only full rescan

known_limits: Timing is an isolated synthetic warm-cache fixture; no cold-cache latency or resident-RAM claim.
Strict mmap-time varint validation adds CPU at load (fixture: raw 0.8244 ms vs compressed 4.7944 ms).
New binary can read old bases; old <=v11 binary rejects v12, so rollback must restore compatible bases/manifests/binary/WAL together.
Production conversion, deployment and actual-byte reduction are owned and recorded by the main agent separately.
